[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Pleasant Pairs** [CF 1541B · Pleasant Pairs](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1541/B){rating="1200"}

The condition ties a **product of values** to a **sum of indices**, and no rearrangement separates it into "a key of $i$ equals a key of $j$" as in @sec-cnt-pidx-message. What saves us is size: $i + j \le 2n - 1$, so only pairs with $a_i \cdot a_j < 2n$ can ever qualify. Fix $i$; then $j$ must make $i + j$ a multiple of $a_i$, i.e. $j \equiv -i \pmod{a_i}$, so the candidates are $j = a_i - i,\ 2a_i - i,\ 3a_i - i, \ldots$ — about $2n / a_i$ of them. Because the values are **distinct**, $\sum_i 2n/a_i \le 2n(1 + \tfrac12 + \cdots + \tfrac{1}{2n}) = O(n \log n)$: a harmonic sum, the reason the double loop collapses.

[Solved in full in @sec-cnt-pidx-pleasant.]{.card-link}
